items.item: A global 100 GB/month free tier for internet egress, shared across every AWS service and region
An hourly gateway fee plus a per-GB data-processing fee, stacked on top of ordinary transfer charges for the same bytes
Inter-region transfer priced by region pair, not a flat global rate ($0.02/GB North America vs $0.16/GB South America)
Internet egress tiered by monthly volume, falling from $0.087/GB to $0.05/GB past 10 TB
Cross-zone VM-to-VM rate ($0.01/GiB) matches AWS's cross-AZ rate under a different name
Cloud NAT's three-part pricing shape (hourly gateway, per-GiB processing, ordinary egress) mirrors AWS's NAT gateway exactly, down to the same $0.045/GiB processing number

items.item: Two cloud vendors arriving at the identical per-unit price for a conceptually similar boundary (GCP's Cloud NAT and AWS's NAT gateway, both $0.045 per unit processed) is not evidence of a shared cost basis between the vendors; it is a coincidence worth stating as such, not inferring a cause for

Measuring a correctness mechanism's request cost directly (rather than assuming 'safer costs more' or 'safer is free') is the only way to know whether a retry-based fix changed the bill, and this topic's own lab is built specifically to make that measurement real
The four-dimension framing is deliberately cloud-agnostic; the next topic's cross-cloud map depends on this topic never having tied a dimension's name to one vendor's product name
